blocks.c: "At the moment of renewal," I said, "there are two caretakers in occupation of these premises. Wen Aguilar, maintaining the 1994 volume, in continuous use since January 1994. Ravi Oduya, maintaining the current volume, in use since January. Both volumes are the Record under page ten. Both of us are Caretakers under page ten. Neither of us is outgoing, because neither of us has resigned, been substituted, or ceased to maintain."
"The renewal proceeds," I said. "We're not stopping it. Renew. Renew with two caretakers in occupation."

I want to describe that silence properly because it lasted about eleven seconds and it was the loudest thing in my life. It was the silence of a system running a query. Somewhere behind that clerk, in filing cabinets going back further than the wall, a hundred and fifty-one years of paper was being checked for a sentence that said only one, and the sentence was not there, because nobody had ever needed to write it.

"If there are two caretakers in occupation," it said slowly, "then no account settles at renewal, because no caretaker is outgoing. And if no account settles, every held dispute remains held. And if every dispute remains held—"
"Then the boxes stay in the warehouse," said Wen Aguilar. "For another fifty-one years. Say it. Say it out loud, you enormous filing cabinet."
Behind the blind, the grey went to gold.
